name: Myanmar
official: Republic of the Union of Myanmar

facts.religion: Theravada Buddhism about 88%, Christian about 6%, Muslim about 4%

system_note: Coup leader Min Aung Hlaing became president after a junta-run election.
snapshot: The junta held a widely dismissed election and made its leader president, but civil war goes on across much of the country five years after the coup.
culture: Myanmar is overwhelmingly Buddhist, and the golden Shwedagon Pagoda in Yangon and the temples of Bagan are national symbols. Thanaka, a pale bark paste worn on the face, is used by women and children for beauty and sun protection. More than 130 ethnic groups, including the Shan, Karen, Kachin and Rakhine, have their own languages and traditions.
society: Since the 2021 coup, resistance forces and ethnic armies have taken large areas, and the military has responded with air strikes on villages. Millions are displaced, and a March 2025 earthquake killed thousands. In 2017 the army drove some 700,000 Rohingya Muslims into Bangladesh in what the UN called genocidal violence.
situation: On 1 February 2021, the day Myanmar's newly elected parliament was to sit, the army arrested Aung San Suu Kyi, whose party had won 396 of 476 seats, and seized power, claiming fraud. The coup set off a civil war that has killed tens of thousands and displaced millions. Five years later, the general who led it found a way to make his rule look civilian.

After a three-phase election in December and January organised by the junta and dismissed by observers as neither free nor fair, the army-backed Union Solidarity and Development Party dominated a parliament where a quarter of seats are reserved for soldiers. On 3 April, it elected Senior General Min Aung Hlaing president with 429 of 584 votes (AFP via NST). The vote took place in a parliament building in Naypyidaw repaired after the 2025 earthquake. Because the constitution forbids a president from also leading the army, he handed command on 30 March to Ye Win Oo, a former intelligence chief seen as fiercely loyal (Reuters via Chronicle.lu). China, his key ally, promptly congratulated him. Suu Kyi, now 81, remains in prison. Analysts expect the new government to court neighbours for recognition while pressing the war against ethnic armies and resistance forces that still hold large parts of the country.
power: A presidential system under the military-written 2008 constitution. Parliament elects the president; the military holds 25 percent of seats, a veto over constitutional change, and control of the defence, interior and border ministries.
holders: President Min Aung Hlaing, with the army under Commander-in-Chief Ye Win Oo.

update.html: On 18 November President Min Aung Hlaing told parliament that his government had decided to review its future relations with ASEAN, accusing the bloc of unfair treatment, after ASEAN leaders said at their summit in the Philippines that Myanmar had made insufficient progress on the 2021 five-point peace plan. ASEAN still keeps Myanmar's top leaders out of its main summits. He said Myanmar would keep talking to individual members and hold a peace conference in February.

story: The Bagan kingdom built thousands of temples. Britain conquered Burma in the 19th century. Independent in 1948, it fell to a military coup in 1962. Aung San Suu Kyi led the democracy movement and spent 15 years under house arrest. The army allowed elections from 2010 and her party won in 2015, but in 2021 the army seized power again, setting off a nationwide civil war. The army's 2017 campaign drove 700,000 Rohingya into Bangladesh.
